<reflection>
The 10x lower catalyst experiment now separates some mechanisms:
- M3 (dimer-active catalyst) is now best fit, suggesting sub-linear catalyst scaling
- M4 (alternate catalytic species X) got much worse (-23.7), essentially ruled out
- M5, M20 also worse
- Most other mechanisms still cluster together

The catalyst order test partially worked. Still need to discriminate among top mechanisms: M3, M7, M6/M8, M2, M1 cluster.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Key remaining discriminators:
- **M3 (2cat dimerization, dimer is active)**: rate has strong [cat]^2 at low cat, saturates at high cat
- **M2 (dimer as reservoir, monomer active)**: dimerization reduces effective monomer, so rate scales sub-linearly at high [cat]
- **M7 (substrate-substrate on catalyst, catS2 active)**: rate should increase with [S]^2 at low S
- **M6, M8 (catalyst activation)**: initial lag phase possible
- **M1 (simple MM)**: linear in cat, saturable in S

Best next test: HIGH catalyst concentration. This will:
- M3: saturate (dimer is dominant, rate approaches k2*[cat_total]/2)
- M2: sub-linear scaling due to dimer sequestration
- M1: linear scaling, full conversion
- M6/M8: no lag if [cat]/[cat*] equilibrium fast; rate scales linearly
- M7: proportional to cat

Also to probe substrate order (M7), we could vary [S], but a high catalyst run with moderate substrate should sharply distinguish dimerization effects.

Propose: [S]=1.0, [cat]=0.05 (5x higher than run 1), [P]=0. This should reveal saturation curvature in cat.
</hypothesis>
